title: SYSK Selects: How Pez Works
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the October 2015 episode "How Pez Works." Josh and Chuck (with guest producer Noel) open with personal banter about liking Pez candy, then cover Pez history: Austrian confectioner Eduard Haas III's peppermint candy marketed as a smoking-cessation aid, the name origin from the German word for peppermint, employee Oskar Uxa's cigarette-lighter-style dispenser, the move to America and the addition of heads and cartoon characters in the 1950s-60s, flavors, and the Pez Girls. They then discuss the late-1980s collecting craze, licensed and special dispensers (Santa, bicentennial figures, Orange County Chopper, Gene Simmons), the Pez Collector's museum in Burlingame, California, and the 'Pez Outlaw' Steve Glew who bought dispensers in Eastern Europe and was undercut by Mark McGwire's... (as stated, Scott McGwinnie's Pez company). The episode closes with a listener email from animator Margie about college debt and not needing a degree for some jobs.

segments.title: Opening banter about Pez
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck, introducing the Selects episode, chat about how they eat Pez, the taste of orange Pez, Lego-style candy bricks, and factory tours.

segments.title: Pez facts and royal wedding dispensers
segments.summary: They cite sugar and production figures (fifty thousand pounds of sugar every four days, three thousand pounds of pressure, twelve million tablets a day in Orange, Connecticut), mention a royal wedding dispenser sold for charity, and the most expensive dispenser sold on eBay, a 2006 astronaut edition for thirty-two thousand dollars. They note eBay founder Pierre Omidyar's link to Pez collecting.

segments.title: Eduard Haas III and the origin of Pez
segments.summary: Austrian confectioner Eduard Haas III, a germophobe and anti-smoking advocate, made peppermint mints sold as smoking-cessation aids; the name Pez derives from the German word for peppermint.

segments.title: Oskar Uxa's dispenser and the American launch
segments.summary: Employee Oskar Uxa designed a cigarette-lighter-style dispenser that popped out one candy at a time, which made Pez a hit in Europe and then in the United States with kids.

segments.title: Pez Girls, flavors and the switch to toys
segments.summary: Discussion of the Pez Girls marketing figures, the peach flavor never released in the US, the chlorophyll flavor, and the move to character heads to make the product more parent-friendly, along with sugar sticks and other candies.

segments.title: Pez collecting craze and licensed dispensers
segments.summary: Collecting took off in the late 1980s; the hosts discuss reloadable licensed dispensers (Looney Tunes, Star Wars, Hello Kitty), Make a Face Pez, the bicentennial series, Santa and Halloween designs, feet added in 1987, and celebrity dispensers like Orange County Chopper and Gene Simmons.

segments.title: Pez museum, vitamins and the Pez Outlaw
segments.summary: The Pez Museum in Burlingame, California grew out of a computer dealership; Pez tried vitamins briefly; and Steve Glew, the so-called Pez Outlaw, bought unlicensed dispensers in Eastern Europe, was undercut by Pez's own counterfeit-style releases, and was driven out of business, as told in a Playboy article.

segments.title: Listener mail: college and student loans
segments.summary: Listener Margie, an animator, writes that many jobs are learned on the job rather than requiring college degrees and that she is still paying off student loans; the hosts discuss the stigma around college.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts give contact info and the show's website, and close the episode.
